situation: After image_drop and a battery pull the camera produced no USB enumeration and no display, the third brick of this investigation.

declined_option.proposal: write factory /usr (nflasha15) and /etc (nflasha10) images over fastboot
declined_option.why_declined: Wrong diagnosis. The WBI header was still zero from image_drop, so Loader2 had no snapshot to restore and never reached the kernel at all; /usr and /etc contents were never consulted during boot. Rewriting 249 MB and 12 MB of partitions would have changed nothing about the failure while costing hours of flash time and a large new risk surface.

what_was_actually_wrong: Only nflasha5 sector 0. It was zeroed on purpose by image_drop, and with a zero header none of Loader2's four predicates match, so the camera does not reach a display.
recovery_steps: Pico inject stage1 (prebuilt/stage1.bin), fastboot appears as 18d1:4ee0 in about 57 s
host/bootstrap.py loads stage2-flash-20261026 and verifies eMMC (emmc-init rc 0, 30 partitions)
restore_zero_header.py --dry-run: gate 1 (bytes 0..511 all zero) and gate 2 (bytes 512..4095 match archive) both OK
restore_zero_header.py: wrote 512 bytes at LBA 180224, readback byte-exact
state_after: fastboot reboot issued; the camera then enumerated as 054c:0994 (charging mode), which is the PID a Sony body shows over USB while it is powered off or charging. No agent yet.
lesson: The WBI header is the single point of failure for boot on this camera and it is reachable without any partition rewrite. Restore it first, always, before considering /usr or /etc work.
